headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here are a few well‑known public APIs that accept an IP address and return detailed company‑level information (including contact details when available). All of them offer free tiers with rate limits, and paid plans for higher usage or more fields. | API | Key Features | Free Tier | Paid Plans | Notes | |-----|--------------|-----------|------------|-------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Company name, domain, AS number, and contact email.
• Geo‑location, carrier, and organization details.
• Supports bulk lookups via CSV upload. | 50k requests/month, 1 request/sec | $5–$25/month for higher limits and additional fields (e.g., phone, website). | Very easy to use; JSON response. | | **ipstack.com** | • Organization name, domain, and contact email.
• Geo‑location, currency, and timezone.
• Supports IPv6. | 10k requests/month, 1 request/sec | $9–$99/month for higher limits and extra fields (e.g., phone, website). | Good for real‑time lookup; offers a “Business” plan with more data. | | **ipapi.co** | • Organization name, domain, and contact email.
• Geo‑location, carrier, and ASN.
• Supports bulk lookups via CSV. | 30k requests/month, 1 request/sec | $9–$49/month for higher limits and additional fields (e.g., phone, website). | Simple REST endpoint; free tier includes most fields. | | **ipdata.co** | • Company name, domain, and contact email.
• Geo‑location, carrier, ASN, and threat intelligence.
• Bulk lookup via CSV. | 50k requests/month, 1 request/sec | $5–$25/month for higher limits and extra fields (e.g., phone, website). | Offers a “Premium” plan with more data and higher limits. | | **ipgeolocation.io** | • Organization name, domain, and contact email.
• Geo‑location, carrier, ASN, and threat intelligence.
• Bulk lookup via CSV. | 30k requests/month, 1 request/sec | $9–$49/month for higher limits and additional fields (e.g., phone, website). | Good for real‑time lookup; free tier includes most fields. | ### How to Use (Example with ipinfo.io) ```bash curl https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8?token=YOUR_TOKEN ``` Response: ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` If you have a paid plan, you’ll also get fields like `company`, `phone`, `website`, and `email`. ### Choosing the Right Plan - **Free Tier**: Good for low‑volume projects or testing. Usually limited to ~10k–50k requests/month. - **Paid Plans**: Needed if you require higher request rates, bulk lookups, or additional fields such as phone numbers and websites. Prices vary from $5 to $99 per month depending on the provider and features. ### Things to Keep in Mind 1. **Rate Limits**: All providers enforce a per‑second limit (typically 1 request/sec). Exceeding this will result in temporary bans. 2. **Data Accuracy**: Contact information is only available for corporate IP ranges. Residential IPs usually return no company data. 3. **Privacy & Compliance**: Ensure you comply with GDPR and other privacy regulations when storing or processing IP data. --- #### Quick Start If you just want to test one of these services, sign up for a free account at any of the links above, grab your API key, and try the curl command shown. Once you’re comfortable, you can integrate the chosen API into your application using your preferred programming language (Python, Node.js, Java, etc.).
